claims.statement: The forward process gradually adds Gaussian noise with a fixed schedule; x_t can be sampled from x_0 in closed form (Eq. 4).
The network predicts the added noise epsilon; training minimizes ||epsilon - epsilon_theta(x_t, t)||^2 with t uniform in 1..T (Algorithm 1, Eq. 14).
Sampling starts from standard normal noise and iterates t = T..1, adding noise except at the last step (Algorithm 2).
Epsilon prediction makes the model resemble denoising score matching over noise levels, with sampling resembling Langevin dynamics.
Lsimple drops the time-dependent weights of the bound; this de-emphasizes small-t terms and gave better sample quality (not better likelihood).
Ablation: mu-tilde prediction works only with the true bound; learning reverse variances is unstable; epsilon prediction with Lsimple is best.
Log likelihoods (codelengths) are not competitive with other likelihood-based models despite high sample quality.
Most of the lossless codelength describes imperceptible distortions; the model is an excellent lossy compressor (progressive coding).
Sampling is progressive decoding, a generalization of autoregressive decoding; large-scale features appear first, details last (Fig. 6).
Image data scaled linearly to [-1, 1]; the reverse process ends with a discrete decoder.
The CIFAR10 FID 3.17 is unconditional and measured against the training set.
The network is a U-Net based on PixelCNN++ with group normalization; time enters via sinusoidal position embeddings.
Limitations / broader impact: slow sampling (1000 network evaluations), possible misuse for fake images, dataset bias.
